newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hopes troops in Zaire by weekend.
newsitem.headline: France hopes troops in Zaire by weekend.

text.p: France hopes the first troops in a multinational force will be in Zaire by the weekend on a mission strictly limited to aiding starving refugees, its foreign minister said on Thursday.

Herve de Charette said he hoped the U.N. Security Council would approve the force in the coming hours after Washington signalled its agreement in principle to take part in the mission to ensure food, water and medicines reach refugees fleeing fighting in east Zaire.

"I hope that by the weekend we'll see the first soldiers on the ground," de Charette told Europe 1 radio. France is ready to send 600 paratroopers within 24 hours of U.N. approval and 600 more within 48 hours, defence officials said.

De Charette said the force's sole task should be to ensure aid gets to 1.2 million Hutu refugees from Rwanda and Burundi. He rejected suggestions that it should, for instance, help repatriate refugees or seek to control Tutsi rebels.
"All these are questions in which I think the multinational force, the peace force, the force of humanitarian aid, should not get involved," he said.

"Today I will meet the Americans and the Canadians to work on the details," de Charette said. U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy were in Paris on Thursday for a peace summit on Bosnia.
De Charette reiterated Paris' calls for a peace summit for countries in Africa's Great Lakes region to seek a longer-term political solution to conflicts including genocide in Rwanda in 1994.
"It's urgent to treat the symptoms, but we must also cure the illness," de Charette said.

Rwanda accuses France of being partisan after it sent 2,500 troops to Rwanda in 1994 to help stop Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis and moderate Hutus. Rwanda's government says the French operation helped Hutus escape to Zaire.
De Charette said "terrible crimes" had been committed in Rwanda in 1994 and that "those who committed them must be lawfully tried."
